start.content: I was there that morning, having come from Cana with the others. The women had already told us about the empty tomb. We had seen the risen Lord twice in Jerusalem. But Peter said he was going fishing. Seven of us went with him.

choices.text: What did you observe on the water?
What was Peter's state of mind?

observation.content: We fished all night and caught nothing. At dawn a man stood on the shore and called out to cast on the right side. We cast, and the net filled so fast we could not haul it. A hundred and fifty-three large fish, and the net held. John recognised Him first and said, "It is the Lord." Peter jumped in immediately.

choices.text: The same miracle as when He first called them.

response.content: Peter was quiet on the water. Not the Peter who argues with everyone — subdued. Three denials beside a fire still had their weight on him. He had seen the risen Lord in Jerusalem. He believed. But believing and being forgiven are not always the same moment.

first_calling.content: Yes. On the Sea of Galilee three years before. A boat, empty nets, cast on the right side, then an overwhelming catch. It was not subtle. He was giving them — giving Peter — the same sign that began everything. Only now it was ending something, or beginning it again differently.

shore_scene.content: He had a charcoal fire burning on the beach. Bread and fish cooking. The risen Lord — preparing breakfast. We dragged the net ashore and He invited us to eat. We all knew who He was. No one asked. After we ate, He turned to Peter.

charcoal_fire.content: Peter denied Him three times in the High Priest's courtyard beside a charcoal fire — John 18:18, a charcoal fire is specifically mentioned. On this beach, another charcoal fire. He built the setting deliberately. Same fire, same number of questions. Not to punish — to restore. The wound was made beside a fire; the healing was made beside a fire.

peter_commission.content: Three times He asked: "Do you love me?" The first two times Peter answered "agapao" — the higher love. The third time Jesus used Peter's own word back at him — "phileo" — the brotherly love. Peter was grieved on the third question. He understood the pattern. He said, "Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you." Each answer received the same commission: "Feed my lambs. Tend my sheep. Feed my sheep."

choices.text: He was not accused. Just asked.

restoration.content: Restored and commissioned. Three denials, three questions, three reinstatements. Then Jesus said: "Follow me." The exact words He used at the beginning beside the Sea of Galilee. Three years, a death, a resurrection, and it ends with the same two words. Follow me. I think that was the whole point. It was never about achievement. It was always about following.

choices.text: A precise repair for a precise wound.

grace_pattern.content: He did not demand an explanation. He did not rehearse the failures. He asked one question — love — and built everything on the answer. Three times, because the wound required three. The architecture of the forgiveness matched the architecture of the failure. That kind of precision is not human management. That is something else.

choices.text: What did Peter's face look like after?

closing.content: Like a man who had been carrying something for three days and had just been given permission to put it down. He wept on the third question. Then Jesus said follow me and Peter stood up and followed and his face was the face of someone who had just received back something they had given up expecting to have again.
